title: TypeScript 6 vs 7 on type-fest
question: How much faster does TypeScript 7 type-check a real, type-heavy library, and how much of the gain comes from parallel checking rather than the native compiler itself?
verdict: Open until measured on more machines. In the reference environment (1 core, 4 GB), TypeScript 7 checked the library sources about 3 times faster with lower memory, and the full suite with type tests ran out of memory with both compilers.
takeaway: Measure TypeScript 7 on your own project and your own CI runners: the gain depends on cores and memory, not just on the compiler.
notes: Types and Instantiations differ between TypeScript 6 and 7 on identical code. The two compilers may not count the same way, so do not compare these counters across compilers without checking how each one counts.
